mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC weekly declines are decelerating (-5.6, then -1.9, then -2.0 points), indicating the pool of still-suppressible in-person retail activity is being exhausted; the next 28-day mean therefore prints above the last 28-day mean, which contains the steepest single-week collapse.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly changes -5.6, -1.9, -2.0 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC weekly declines re-accelerate (any weekly drop exceeding the prior week's drop by more than 1 point) and the next-28-day mean is below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has held at or above +25 for three straight weeks (+28.0, +28.4, +29.0), so time-at-home is saturated and household errand capacity is fully organized around essential trips; further suppression of RETAIL_REC is bounded, making the next 28-day mean higher than the last.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean at or above +25 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reads 28.0, 28.4, 29.0 over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL holds above +25 while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are falling jointly (-80.0 and -71.9), but their joint week-on-week step has compressed to about 1 point from roughly 6 points three weeks earlier; once the two commuter series stop draining together, the retail catchment stops shrinking and RETAIL_REC rises.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both change by less than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: Joint TRANSIT-WORKPLACES flattening occurs while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays below the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT keeps printing successive weekly lows (-70.3, -76.9, -79.0, -80.0), so the mobility contraction is still propagating through the system; each further transit step-down shrinks the reachable retail catchment, driving the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls by at least 0.5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declines in every week of the snapshot window
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls another full point or more but the next four RETAIL_REC weekly means average above the last four.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal spring warming across late April and May lifts outdoor activity in Manhattan; once PARKS turns up from its -67.7 trough, discretionary trip minutes substitute into open-air space rather than enclosed retail, holding the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -67.7 on t-0w, below its -60.3 level on t-3w
failure_condition: PARKS rises more than 3 points week-on-week while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Non-essential business closure mandates remain in force for the entire four-week horizon, freezing RETAIL_REC at its trough; because the last 28 days contain the steepest descent, a flat suppressed next window still yields a higher mean than the prior window.
candidate_trigger: closure order covering non-essential retail stays in force for the full 28-day horizon
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC falls 9.5 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Closure mandates remain in force yet the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean falls below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The 37-point gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-49.9) and RETAIL_REC (-86.9) marks essential-anchored trips that are still occurring; as stockpiling fades and GROCERY_PHARM stops declining, those trips spill into pharmacy-anchored and adjacent retail formats, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change at or above -1 point
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes while the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean remains below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL keeps setting new weekly highs (+24.9, +28.0, +28.4, +29.0), meaning household time is still being redirected out of commercial space; each additional half point of home confinement suppresses discretionary trips, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the last.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean sets a new high at least 0.5 points above the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions in all four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL sets a new weekly high at least 0.5 points above the prior week while the next four RETAIL_REC weekly means average above the last four.
